Treat- ment for endocarditis should continue for 28 days. • USA: • parenteral ceftriaxone 1 g every 24 hours alternatives are: • intravenous ceftizoxime 1 g every 8 hours • cefotaxime 1 g every 8 hours • intramuscular spectinomycin 2 g every 12 hours Once improvement has been established for 24 to 48 hours, oral therapy with cefixime 400 mg twice daily, or cefpodoxime 400 mg twice daily may be substitut- ed until at least a 1-week treatment period is com- plete. Provided antimicrobial susceptibility is docu- mented fluoroquinolones may be given as an alternative treatment. For gonococcal meningitis and endocarditis, intrave- nous ceftriaxone 1 to 2 g every 12 hours is recom- mended; treatment for meningitis should continue for 10 to 14 days and for endocarditis for at least 4 weeks. 192 Antibacterials • GONOCOCCAL INFECTIONS IN NEONATES AND CHILDREN. Neonates born to mothers with gonorrhoea are at high risk of infection and require prophylaxis: • WHO: • a single intramuscular injection of ceftriaxone 50 mg/kg (maximum 125 mg) alternatives are: • a single intramuscular dose of spectinomycin 25 mg/kg (maximum 75 mg) • a single intramuscular dose of kanamycin 25 mg/kg (max- imum 75 mg) • USA: • a single parenteral dose of ceftriaxone 25 to 50 mg/kg (maximum 125 mg) For those neonates with disseminated gonococcal infec- tion (sepsis, arthritis, meningitis), US recommendations are: • parenteral ceftriaxone 25 to 50 mg/kg once daily for 7 days, or • parenteral cefotaxime 25 mg/kg every 12 hours for 7 days Treatment should be extended to 10 to 14 days if meningitis is present. Treatment for children with uncomplicated gonococcal infections, most commonly due to sexual abuse in pre- adolescents, is as for adults in those weighing 45 kg or more. For those weighing less than 45 kg a single intra- muscular dose of ceftriaxone 125 mg or spectinomycin 40 mg/kg (maximum 2 g) is recommended. For dissem- inated infection in all children an intramuscular or intra- venous dose of ceftriaxone 50 mg/kg once daily for 7 days, up to a maximum dose of 1 g in those weighing less than 45 kg is recommended. The prevention and treatment of neonatal gonococcal con- junctivitis is discussed under Neonatal Conjunctivitis, p.180.
